column2: A small body of water where ducks act like the homeowners and mosquitoes run the HOA.
A thin metal bar or flexible twig; material for fences and old-school literary discipline.
A tiny skin bump that has a sixth sense for showing up right before an important meeting.
A single lock of hair that the wind selects for an impromptu solo performance.
Knitting thread that patient hands turn into sweaters, socks, and bragging rights.
A woman who spins thread; a master at turning raw fiber into future wardrobe staples.
An attendant for hunting hounds who has way more dog chores than your average pet owner.
A specialist who helps untangle your thoughts and feelings without consulting a crystal ball.
A feathered creature that gets to travel by air with no ticket and zero regard for schedules.
A stiff-toed ballet shoe that lets a dancer stand on tiptoe and somehow keep smiling.
A homemade or antique noisemaker weapon that sounds way scarier than it looks.
An old Russian weight unit of about 16 kilograms; a heavy hello from pre-metric days.
Loose or pressed makeup that convinces your face you actually had a good morning.
Rhythmic throbs in your arteries; an internal metronome that speeds up when the repair bill arrives.
A large wild cat that won't purr in your lap or meow for you to open the door.
A warm, spiced mixed drink; a party guest that arrives with a recipe big enough for the whole crowd.
A tiny mark on your belly left over from when you were still plugged into Mom.
A fierce snowstorm with howling wind; weather so wild even the snowdrifts lose their sense of direction.
The start of a machine or process; the exact moment you press the button and hope kicks in.
A vast arid expanse where water is worth far more than pretty promises.
A road or route toward a goal—sometimes short on the map, endless on foot.
Soft, weightless feathers or fluff; the stuff clouds appear to be made of.
A dense, untamed primeval forest where your GPS starts speaking in riddles.
A striped worker who gathers nectar and genuinely doesn't get why humans panic at her work ethic.
Hulled grain that cooks up into a sunny-colored porridge with plenty of personality.
A stubborn weed with sprawling roots; a garden tenant that refuses to take eviction hints.
A dramatic script written for the stage that only comes alive once actors stop reading it.
Someone who overindulges in alcohol and lets the bottle substitute for common sense a bit too often.
An old unit of length—the distance between the tips of your stretched thumb and index finger.
The back part of your foot, and always the first to find out your new shoes are uncomfortable.
A smudge or discolored spot; a tiny mishap that looks like front-page news on a white shirt.
A person stripped of freedom and subject to another's will; the polar opposite of independence.
Someone who straps on a scuba tank and considers the ocean floor a great place for a stroll.
An activity people usually pay you for—and occasionally the thing haunting your thoughts all weekend.
A device that spots objects using radio waves; an electronic eye that never needs glasses.
An Indian prince or ruler; a title historically bundled with power and a lavish court.
A radioactive element discovered by the Curies; best kept glowing strictly inside textbooks.
A device transmitting sound over distance; a chatty companion that never interrupts and picks all the music.
A radioactive inert gas that can build up indoors and demands serious respect.
The capacity to think and decide; an inner advisor frequently drowned out by impulse.
A place of eternal bliss; the ultimate vacation where checking your email isn't even an option.
A section of a city or territory with its own borders, addresses, and local quirks.
A strong Balkan fruit brandy; a cultural tradition best served in very small glasses.
A demonic being in Hindu mythology rarely cast as the friendly neighbor in fairy tales.
A border around a painting, window, or door that helps everything look pulled together.
A border for a photo or certificate that announces, 'This matters—hang it on the wall.'
A sloped walkway for going up or down; a wheel-friendly alternative to stairs.
An unpleasant reminder that skin isn't armor—and the last place you want anyone rubbing salt.
A level of distinction or official standing; a spot in the hierarchy that doesn't always match one's ego.
A rigid-backed school backpack; a portable warehouse for textbooks and squished sandwiches.
A reinforced strip along the edge of a shoe sole that helps a boot keep its shape.
An oilseed crop with bright yellow fields; agriculture's way of painting the spring.
An archaic word for an army or armed troop, straight out of heroic epics.
A single stage of a boxing match or contest; the stretch of time before athletes get a breather.
A formal evening reception where polite small talk runs strictly on schedule.
A bone-mineralization disorder mostly affecting children; a medical topic for doctors, not jokes.
A handheld two-way radio; a phone that doesn't care if there's a cell tower in sight.
Torn, worn-out clothes or tatters; a wardrobe that is long overdue for retirement.
An aquatic plant thriving in ponds and rivers; a green houseplant that skipped the pot.
A small human with big questions, boundless energy, and a magnetic attraction to puddles.
A curved chest bone protecting vital organs—and, according to ancient sources, the raw material for women.
A puzzle hiding words behind pictures and symbols, testing the solver's patience.
A deep, booming sound produced by an engine, a wild beast, or an outraged neighbor.
A crisp, crimson root vegetable with a peppery kick that makes zero apologies for its spice.
A field fortification for defense; the military version of a castle minus the palace perks.
An established schedule or order of actions that your body appreciates far more than chaos.
A cutting tool or a front tooth—either way, designed to neatly slice off a piece.
A sound reason or valid argument; what shows up in a debate when emotion briefly yields to logic.
A long, narrow strip of wood; a humble piece that often saves a complex build.
A scheduled trip or air journey; a single line item on a transit timetable.
A natural flowing watercourse that never asks permission before cutting across the landscape.
A steel track guiding train wheels; a road a locomotive is wise not to argue with.
A tiny titmouse famous for weaving an intricate pouch-shaped hanging nest.
A rare, dense metal with a sky-high melting point that is in no hurry to become a liquid.
Regular income from capital or property; money that arrives without necessarily bringing a Monday with it.
A root vegetable made famous by a classic fairy tale about teamwork at harvest time.
An establishment where food is cooked and served; you arrive hungry and leave with memories and a bill.
A small river; a waterway of modest scale that still packs plenty of charm.
A chosen course of action; the moment your overthinking finally stops walking in circles.
A horizontal spar on a sailing ship's mast from which a square sail hangs.
A light two-wheeled cart—or its driver; city transit where human legs replace the engine.
A raised platform for boxing matches; a square arena where arguments are settled with gloves.
Inflammation of the nasal lining—when your nose suddenly forgets its primary job description.
A staple grain and popular side dish; tiny kernels capable of feeding half the planet.
The chance of an unfavorable outcome; the price of boldness when luck hasn't signed the contract.
A thin line or scratch on a surface; a tiny mark that keeps measurements honest.
An alternating pattern of sounds or beats; the inner metronome of life and the dance floor.
Matching word endings; a favorite tool of poets and playground counting games.
An automated machine built to handle tasks; a coworker that doesn't ask for paid time off yet.
A long trench dug into the earth, often circling a fort; a defensive ditch with serious tenure.
A hard growth on an animal's head or a brass instrument; occasionally a punchline about unfaithful spouses.
A tall marsh plant topped with brown fuzzy spikes resembling velvet cigars.
Someone tied to you by blood or marriage who still remembers all your childhood nicknames.
A hardy cereal grain milled into flour for fragrant, dark loaves of bread.
A flexible twig used historically for corporal punishment; a teaching aid with a terrible reputation.
A large crowd of insects moving as one; a team where nobody actually appointed a manager.
A low, rolling hum produced by a heavy engine or distant thunder.
A strong spirit distilled from sugarcane; all the romance of pirate novels bottled up.
A quiet expression of discontent; collective grumbling dialed down to minimum volume.
Morning moisture droplets on grass; nature's tiny beads that vanish with the first sunbeams.
An increase in size or simply how tall you are; a metric measured with immense pride in childhood.
A military unit; an organized squad of soldiers sharing a common mission.
The spinning part of a machine; a component that strongly prefers never standing still.
A small deciduous woodland; a leafy spot ideal for a stroll and a mental reboot.
A large keyboard instrument; basically a piano that earned its own dedicated room.
A metal that stays liquid at room temperature; shiny little droplets you are strictly forbidden to play with.
A boundary or major milestone; the line right after which a brand-new chapter begins.
A precious crimson gemstone that looks like a captured sliver of sunset.
Russia's currency; a wallet regular that undergoes routine stress-testing by inflation.
A long-barreled firearm; an item demanding strict adherence to safety rules.
A human upper limb; an all-purpose tool equally adept at hard work and waving hello.
The part of a garment covering the arm, doubling as a cozy pocket for chilly hands.
A rolled pastry or filled dessert; a delicious way to curl pure joy into a spiral.
Material wound into a cylinder; the standard storage format for paper, wallpaper, and long things.
The wheel controlling a vehicle's direction; the circle you grip when the road starts asking questions.
A compass point; one of the directional sectors used in marine navigation.
An expressive Latin dance; music that can make even a trip to the fridge look dramatic.
A native of Romania; a citizen of a land of Carpathian peaks, castles, and rich history.
A cone-shaped device for amplifying the voice; the original loudhailer before batteries were invented.
The channel along which a river flows; nature's custom-carved water highway.
An American sci-fi and fantasy master best known for penning The Chronicles of Amber.
